question: Did Paul see Jesus?
summary: Paul in 1 Corinthians 9:1 and 15:8 unambiguously claims to have seen Jesus. Acts 9:8 says that when Paul opened his eyes on the Damascus road he saw no man and had to be led by the hand into Damascus. Paul's first-person testimony and Luke's narrative description of the same event contradict each other on what Paul actually saw.

reconcile.connective: Gill reads Acts 9:8's "no man" as Paul's post-vision blindness, distinct from the Christ he says he had already seen.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible presses the plain conflict between Paul's claim to have seen Jesus and Luke's statement that he "saw no man."

pd_work.note: Clarke poses the question directly — 'whether Jesus Christ did really appear to Saul on this occasion' — and resolves it by appeal to Paul's own words in 1 Cor 9:1 and 15:8, which he says 'put the subject out of dispute.'

excerpts.attribution: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63)
excerpts.excerpt_text: …and when his eyes were opened he saw no man; neither Christ, who appeared to him from heaven, whom he had before seen, nor even any of his companions, nor indeed any object …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill glosses Acts 9:8's 'saw no man' as covering Christ too, but explicitly notes Paul 'had before seen' him — directly reconciling the verse with Paul's own claim in 1 Cor 9:1/15:8 to have seen Jesus.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And Saul arose from the earth,.... As he was bid by Christ, Act 9:6
and when his eyes were opened he saw no man; neither Christ, who appeared to him from heaven, whom he had before seen, nor even any of his companions, nor indeed any object: the Syriac version renders it, "he saw nothing"; not anything at all; and the Ethiopic version, "he could not see": when he opened his eye lids, he perceived his sight was gone, and this showed it to be real blindness; and which was an emblem of the ignorance and blindness he had been in:
but they led him by the hand; the men that were with him, perceiving that he could not guide himself, took him by the hand, and led him on his journey;
and brought him into Damascus; and now was fulfilled, at least in part, the prophecy in Zac 9:1.
